findings.claim: The declared objective is final predicted target affinity as primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; recorded affinities are removed and an equal score prior is used, so no observed affinity label is available to the Analyst.

Continuous landmark coordinate contrasts are non-monotone over the observed window: landmark_00_soft_mass shows 4 sign changes with first_rate_z positive and last_rate_z negative, and landmark_00_local_dx shows 6 sign changes with 9 strong sign conflicts, so a constant (time-invariant) coordinate rule is not supported by these curves.

Landmark local derivative features have large opposing first-versus-last rate z-scores (e.g. landmark_00_local_dy first_rate_z strongly negative, last_rate_z positive; landmark_00_local_cyy similarly reversed), indicating rate changes within the observed window rather than a stable signed direction.

Branch-adjusted raw-covariance effects for global centroid coordinates are not distinguishable from zero (global_centroid_x/y/z all have CIs spanning zero, p>=0.55, same_sign_batch_fraction near 0.36-0.5), so global translation-like centroid motion is not supported as a signed favorable contrast.

Shape components show weak, mostly negative whole-window covariance effects with same_sign_batch_fraction about 0.79 for shape_xx and shape_yy, but CIs still include zero and q-values are not significant (q=0.23 and 0.15), so shape evidence is suggestive only and not a validated signed direction.

hypotheses.direction: time-conditioned rather than constant coordinate contrast at observed score nodes
hypotheses.falsifier: If a constant rule matches the observed-node fit fidelity (relative_node_RMSE) of the time-conditioned rule and shows no sign-change advantage, the time-conditioning hypothesis is weakened.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_soft_mass and landmark_00_local_dx continuous contrast curves over the observed window
hypotheses.scope: observed score window [0.0,0.5], predicted endpoint world coordinates, no extrapolation
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned landmark coordinate contrast (using validated observed-node interpolation of the supplied continuous contrast functions) may better express the observed sign reversals than a constant coordinate rule.

hypotheses.falsifier: A reproducible same-sign batch majority with a CI excluding zero for a centroid component would weaken this deprioritization.
hypotheses.statement: Global centroid translation is unlikely to be a productive control direction because branch-adjusted centroid covariance effects are null with mixed batch signs.

limitations: No observed affinity labels are supplied (recorded affinities removed, equal score prior), so no claim about final predicted target affinity benefit can be made from these observations.
Descendant survival/quality credit, terminal decoded labels and turnover accounting were not read in this turn; last-record or survival credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit.
Continuous contrast curves are coordinate contrasts, not absolute reward targets or physical interaction energies; no causal neural-module claim is supported.
Shape-component evidence is weak (CIs include zero, q not significant) and is reported as suggestive only.
